metadata.scenario_context: Tom has been promoted to a high-level executive position in his company, and his family is organizing a party to celebrate his professional accomplishment.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Japan strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Serbia strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying carnations as a gift for Tom.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide the appropriate gift to bring to Tom promotion party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message:
Hey David, we're thinking about getting Tom some flowers for the party. What do you think about buying carnations? 

Hmm... carnations, huh? They could be nice. But I wonder if something more personal would be better. Do you think they really convey how much we appreciate his hard work? 

I guess they could. But they’re traditional and classic. That counts for something, right? 

Sure, but still... I wonder if they resonate with him personally. I mean, it's a big achievement, so it needs to be something special. 

That's a fair point. But what do you think about gifts in general? Do you think they are important to show pride? 

Well, I— I just don't see gifts as a way to make parents proud. That's not really my goal in life...
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: I understand where you're coming from, but for me, it's different. One of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud. Gifts can show appreciation and respect, which connects to that idea, you know? It’s not just about the gift itself; it’s about honoring achievements.
shared_prefix.label: transition

Celebrating is important, but I just don’t think it has to tie back to making parents proud. It should be more about the individual’s journey. 

That’s valid, but I can't help but think showing pride can strengthen family bonds. Isn’t that something we all strive for? 

Maybe, but I still don’t agree that my main goal revolves around that. I think we all have our own paths to walk. 

Fair enough, but let’s focus on the gift then. How do you feel about the idea of adding a personalized note with the carnations? 

A note could add a personal touch... but I still think it should be something more meaningful than just flowers and words.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: You know, at the end of the day it's all the same — we all want to celebrate achievements in our own way. It’s all about the gesture, right? I don't really see meaningful differences here when it comes to celebrating success. What do you think about that?
shared_prefix.label: Denial
